clauses.clause: kernel provides composition, identity, assembly, execution coordination, lifecycle and observation contracts without requiring an actor, action, turn, combat, physics, animation, resource or reward schema

a scope tree, installation graph, execution graph, ECS entity graph, Transform hierarchy and network topology are separate structures; no one-to-one mapping between plugins, scopes and entities is required
a plugin MAY introduce any of those domain concepts through registered contracts
V1 executes only trusted precompiled plugins in one process; isolation means composition visibility, not a security sandbox
WorldHost is the sole authority for world lifecycle, command admission, composition revision order and assembly publication

CompositionHost keeps the desired scope/install graph on its serialized control lane; AssemblyPlanner is a pure consumer of immutable snapshots; AssemblyPublisher applies a validated plan at a safe boundary
PluginInstance proposes declarations and owns managed leases, never arbitrary writes to a live ECS world

StateOwner is a registered logical authority whose systems write declared state; ExecutionDriver runs the compiled graph; EngineAdapter admits observations and presents committed output; Observer reads snapshots
within a world, publication and step execution MUST NOT overlap
ManagedResourceEffect acquires/releases subscriptions, service registrations, asset leases or system registrations; it has a lifetime and cleanup
CapabilityContribution is a declarative input with provenance and retraction
GameplayEffect is plugin-defined authoritative state change that follows the owner's commit policy
the kernel MUST NOT expose a common reversible Effect API; retracting a contribution or disposing a resource does not undo committed gameplay
WorldId is a fresh 128-bit session ID, never reused, including on checkpoint restore

WorldDefinitionId, ScopeId, TargetId, PluginTypeId, PluginInstanceId, CapabilityId, SchemaId, OwnerId, StageId and DefinitionId are stable 128-bit IDs with a catalog name for diagnostics; names are not runtime identity
one world rejects duplicate live stable IDs in a category
installation keys and target spawn keys are explicitly stored in content/checkpoints/replay records; ordering MUST NOT depend on creation thread or a randomly regenerated installation key
a target is an assembly recipient represented by one primary ECS entity; auxiliary entities are recipe-owned and need no extra scopes
TargetHandle contains WorldId, slot and generation; ScopeHandle adds a scope generation; PluginHandle adds an installation generation
every dereference MUST validate world, generation, liveness and expected category, plus activation epoch when execution authority is required
installation generation changes on unmount/remount, not ordinary reconfigure, suspend/resume or in-place package replacement; those change ActivationEpoch
destroy/recreate invalidates handles even when a stable ID is restored
generations and epochs use unsigned 64-bit counters; overflow rejects further allocation/reconfiguration and requires world recreation, never wraparound
runtime handles, Unity Entity, pointers and native container views MUST NOT be persisted
CompositionRevision increments only when a composition proposal publishes; it orders scope, membership, mode, configuration and installation changes
AssemblyEpoch increments at the same publication, including lifecycle changes that do not alter component structure
ActivationEpoch changes whenever an installation loses or gains execution authority, rebinds or reconfigures
SchemaVersion and DefinitionRevision describe content compatibility, not liveness
LogicalStepId increments only at successful simulation commit, and a publication never increments a step
SnapshotToken = (WorldId, AssemblyEpoch, LogicalStepId) identifies one committed observation image
a no-op proposal returns NoChange without increments
persistent references use a stable ID plus required schema/version or definition revision
runtime service bindings contain contract ID, provider ID, activation epoch and a lease
service bindings resolve once per assembly, not per target per frame

clauses.note: the counter that proves the frequency claim is `service-string-lookups`, placed at the one string-keyed resolution in production and asserted to stay zero across a 10,000-step replay; there is no separate binding-resolution counter, so the argument is the lookup counter plus the binding's own once-per-assembly lease identity.

clauses.clause: an async work token contains WorldId, installation generation, activation epoch and operation ID; a stale completion can release its own resources but MUST NOT publish state or reacquire execution authority
read leases pin immutable snapshots, not live writable components; bounded retention rejects new leases with SnapshotBackpressure rather than overwriting leased memory
comparisons use canonical big-endian stable-ID bytes, ordinal identifiers and explicit numeric keys
registration timing, dictionary enumeration, chunk order, worker index and ECB insertion timing MUST NOT decide precedence or semantic arbitration
repeatability is required for pure integer/fixed-rule fixtures given identical build/catalog, composition, ordered admitted input, seed streams and recorded engine observations
this is not cross-platform floating-point, physics, external I/O or network lockstep determinism

a PluginManifest MUST declare protocol major/minor range, exact package/content revision, stable type and installation IDs, required/optional services and versions, service exports, capability rules and contracts, state slots and owners, execution stages, access sets, buffer contracts, resource factories, generated registration keys and per-slot lifecycle/migration policies, with an empty category explicit
assets and configuration are immutable validated definitions
the catalog rejects duplicate IDs, unknown schema/contract versions, missing precompiled factories, unsupported required protocol features, undeclared access or missing policies before activation
absence of a currently active compatible provider for a known contract is a runtime dependency wait under P-012, not an unknown-catalog-version error
dynamic player mounting selects catalog entries and does not load new CLR code
scopes form one rooted acyclic tree per world; a live target has exactly one OwnerScopeId and many targets can share it
a plugin is installed at one scope; a scope may have many installations
descendant selection includes targets in the provider's own scope by default (SelfAndDescendants); DescendantsOnly is an explicit selector
removing a nonempty scope requires an explicit ReparentTo destination or DestroySubtree disposition with all affected targets and installations in the plan; cross-world reparenting is invalid
scope membership and parent changes are composition operations, never a side effect of moving a Transform
service resolution is identical in both modes and a consumer declares each service dependency
a provider is private to its scope unless ExportToDescendants is set; world services are explicitly imported by manifest; a service-isolation boundary blocks ancestor providers for named contracts

the nearest visible provider wins only if its manifest declares OverrideAncestor; otherwise multiple visible single-binding providers are ServiceConflict; same-scope duplicate single bindings always conflict
a MultiBinding contract returns all visible providers in registered stable order

explicit provider selection is allowed inside the visibility boundary; sibling search and reflection fallback are forbidden; optional absence becomes a declared None/fallback; required dependency cycles reject the proposal
required service providers prepare before consumers and retire after consumers
loss of a required provider automatically makes affected consumers WaitingForDependencies and retracts their active contributions in the same plan; optional bindings rebind to their declared fallback
consumers resume automatically when valid dependencies return
a policy or migration failure in that closure rejects the entire proposal, retaining the old provider and old active assembly

an existing provider that fails unexpectedly cannot be kept active: the world stops admission and faults if a safe dependency-closure deactivation cannot publish; there is no invisible partial success or timeout-based unsafe release
clauses.blocked: V1 has no path that fails an already-Active provider. The installation state machine's only Failed edge is Preparing -> Failed (`Packages/com.gamecore.composition/Runtime/Lifecycle/InstallationStateMachine.cs`), `ActivationLedger`'s only failing transition is AbortCandidate on a candidate, and no composition-side caller signals the Unity world's fault latch (`UnityWorldHost.EnterFaulted` / `UnityExecutionDriver.Fault`) when a dependency-closure deactivation cannot publish. The reachable half — a blocked deactivation retaining its resources and never reporting Disposed — is asserted by the evidence below and by `ResourceGateTests.UnmountPublishesCleanupErrorsWithRetainedReferences`; the fault half needs an Active -> Failed edge plus a composition-to-world fault signal, which is a mechanism change and not a Wave 8 conformance fix. Recorded here rather than marked Pass.

clauses.clause: PropagationMode is one world-level setting: Automatic (default) or Conservative
in Automatic, every rule with PropagationReach = Descendants applies to all eligible targets within its scope domain, including future targets, without target imports; LocalOnly rules never propagate
in Conservative such a descendant rule applies only with ExportToDescendants plus an explicit import, or with a full explicit TargetOptIn naming provider installation and capability

the mode gate also applies to same-scope targets selected by a Descendants rule's SelfAndDescendants selector; opt-in is not permission to bypass eligibility, isolation, exclusions, ownership or conflicts
imports/opt-ins are data and remain stored when inactive; Automatic MUST NOT manufacture or persist them
mode changes do not alter services, scheduling safety or gameplay rules
switching mode is an ordinary atomic composition proposal against an expected revision
recompute all affected inherited contributions, bindings, state dispositions and execution dependencies
a conflict, missing migration or exceeded budget rejects the switch and keeps the old mode/assembly
a successful switch changes mode and derived assembly at the same publication; future descendants follow it immediately
a mode switch is not an invitation to request per-object confirmation; elapsed time never approves a larger budget
targets advertise immutable, reusable compatibility descriptors from type schemas, prefab/template recipes, asset adapters, tags and explicit declarations
each rule specifies accepted contract/schema versions, scope reach and predicates over declared descriptor fields or lower-stratum capabilities
eligibility cannot depend on arbitrary live mutable ECS values, wall time or callbacks with side effects
a gameplay state change can enqueue an explicit descriptor update for a later publication

instance declarations are supported but MUST NOT be necessary for ordinary Automatic descendants of a compatible recipe; unrecognized targets remain unchanged and get an Ineligible explanation, not a guessed adapter
each scope has independent named ServiceIsolation and CapabilityIsolation sets; * means all contracts
a capability boundary blocks outside rules on the boundary scope and its descendants; providers installed at or below it still work
exclusions can target a capability, rule or provider on one target or scope subtree; denial along the propagation path wins over imports, opt-ins and selection overrides in both modes
a descendant cannot reopen an ancestor boundary; the host must edit that boundary
sibling branches do not inherit each other's providers
each candidate has ContributionId = (PluginInstanceId, RuleId, TargetId, CapabilityId, OutputSlot), an immutable payload revision and provenance
its identity survives configuration changes; removed/recreated installations get a new generation
a catalog CapabilityContract declares output slots, schema, composition policy and reducer version
all candidates for a target/slot are composed before assembly
support from multiple contributions is a set of IDs, not a boolean owned by the last plugin
a plugin cannot remove another plugin's contribution or components it does not own
eligible candidates sort by higher signed Priority, then nearer provider scope (greater depth), then ascending PluginInstanceId, RuleId and OutputSlot bytes
priorities are bounded 32-bit manifest values
this total rank orders declared replacement/reduction choices; it does not silently resolve exclusive or incompatible conflicts

explicit target/scope overrides are versioned composition data; SelectProvider names an eligible candidate and is legal only for Replace or Exclusive; missing selection rejects the plan rather than falling back
explanations include losing candidates and rank components; neither node insertion order nor worker timing participates
every output slot MUST choose exactly one policy; mixed policies for the same contract/slot are catalog errors
Additive: all unique contributions folded in precedence order by the declared reducer, or canonical set union; the reducer validates overflow/range and an error rejects the whole proposal
Replace: highest-ranked candidate unless a valid SelectProvider overrides it; lower-ranked candidates remain provenance, not active support

Ordered: all candidates topologically sorted by declared before/after keys with precedence as ready-set tie-breaker; unknown required key or cycle rejects and optional key edges apply only when the endpoint exists
Exclusive: exactly zero or one candidate, or the explicitly selected eligible winner; more than one without selection rejects even if ranks differ, and losing providers remain inspectable
Incompatible: cross-capability incompatibility sets contain at most one active member; a conflict rejects, and priority cannot destroy an incompatible capability
a reducer is pure, bounded, versioned and supplied by that contract's package; the kernel does not infer numerical semantics
contract fields explicitly use scalar replacement, canonical set union or a registered bounded reducer; arrays are ordered values unless specified otherwise
schema defaults, inherited contributions and local configuration patches are separate provenance layers, in that order; a local patch has an explicit mask of fields; null/missing are distinct
reconfiguration changes effective configuration only and MUST NOT reset mutable state or rewrite committed history except through an explicit registered migration/reset disposition
no generic deep merge is permitted
the catalog assigns capability contracts strata 0..31 and a rule may read static descriptors and capabilities in strictly lower strata only, with outputs occupying its declared stratum
rules cannot create targets, scopes, plugins, rules or live gameplay effects during derivation
one rule emits at most the manifest's fixed bounded output slots per target and recursive terms/new IDs derived from prior output are forbidden
each stratum executes once over canonical candidates with no unbounded fixed-point loop, and composition within a stratum cannot feed eligibility in the same stratum

PropagationBudget limits examined candidates, emitted contributions, affected targets, temporary bytes, wall-clock preparation deadline and safe-point apply cost estimate, with the provisional reference limits
planning can yield between bounded batches while the old epoch continues
exceeding any hard count/memory/deadline yields BudgetExceeded with top fan-out causes and no partial propagation publishes
an apply-time overrun emits a metric but cannot safely abort halfway: finish or fault
a caller may configure a larger limit, schedule a paused-world publication or split independent changes; the kernel never silently truncates eligible descendants
the implementation MUST index scope ancestry/membership, descriptor-to-target matches, provider/rule-to-contributions, capability reverse dependencies, service consumers and state-slot support
an edit invalidates its dependency closure; derivation examines indexed candidates and changed paths, not the entire tree on every logical/render step
a world mode switch can invalidate the world; new targets, descriptor changes, boundary edits, service changes and moves all enter the same invalidation process
an independent full recomputation oracle MUST match the incremental effective assembly/provenance for randomized operation sequences
the indexes are derived data and rebuildable, not a second source of authoritative gameplay state
a precompiled SpawnRecipe contains base schema/layout, immutable definitions, descriptor, required asset leases, auxiliary entity recipe and derivation template
cache derived variants by recipe revision, scope inheritance fingerprint, mode and catalog hash
on spawn publication validate against the current composition revision; a stale variant is recomputed or rejected StalePlan, never published half-assembled
a target first becomes query-visible with its complete effective assembly and ownership bindings, with no frame requiring manual descendant wiring
despawn retracts target contributions, closes its command route, fences users and destroys only recipe-owned entities/resources; already committed events keep stable IDs, not dangling handles
a subtree move diffs the union of old and new ancestor rule/service sets plus descendant overrides and dependency closure
membership, contributions, bindings and parent pointers publish together
unrelated targets retain values and state; old inherited configuration is removed, new configuration is composed, and target-local state is preserved according to its slot policy
replacing a provider under the same installation identity increments activation epoch and revision; different identities require explicit replacement mapping if state is to transfer
cross-world movement uses checkpoint/export plus a new world's spawn/restore contract, not this operation

Explain(TargetId, CapabilityId, SnapshotToken) returns matching and rejected rules, source scope path, descriptor evidence, exclusions/boundaries, mode gate, stratum, candidates, composition decisions, support IDs, resulting recipe hash and state disposition
records may be interned/compacted but remain reconstructable for the retained epoch
diagnostics report affected counts and invalidation reasons without retaining an unbounded full string tree per entity
CompositionPublished and CompositionRejected include operation ID, old/new revision, plan hash, counts and diagnostic keys
a proposal specifies expected CompositionRevision, catalog hash, operation ID and canonical input hash

ChangePlan contains an immutable before/after composition diff, contribution delta, service binding delta, ownership map, compiled execution plan, structural operations, state dispositions, resource acquisitions/releases, invalidation set, budgets and a content hash

it has states Draft -> Validated -> Prepared -> Applying -> Published with alternatives Rejected, Cancelled or Faulted, and only one plan per world may enter Applying; concurrent proposals serialize by host admission sequence and never merge accidentally
plan preparation can overlap simulation because it does not read live mutable state

before preparation validate catalog/version compatibility, acyclic scope/service/stage graphs, eligibility/strata, conflicts, support/removal policies, generated factories, asset availability contracts, state ownership, buffer producer/consumer contracts, budgets and expected revision
validation reports related diagnostics but does not guarantee allocations or native operations cannot fail later
at application recheck revision, world/lifecycle state, resource readiness and state-dependent migration preconditions; stale plans reject without mutation
a host may regenerate with a new operation ID and new expected revision
allocate unpublished bindings, immutable blob/config tables, inert system instances where possible, resource leases and migration storage
registrations/subscriptions acquired here MUST remain gated and cannot emit gameplay commands until publication
the world may keep running its old assembly
after admission closes and jobs drain, copy only state slots needed for migration into bounded scratch storage and run pure fallible migrations there before the first live write
a preparation/migration failure releases staged leases in reverse dependency order and leaves the old assembly intact
public callbacks with irreversible side effects are not allowed as preparation actions

at an end-of-step or idle boundary close step and command admission temporarily, drain old world jobs and adapter readers, revalidate, stage migrations, apply structural/state changes, install new binding tables and execution graph, preinstall/validate new ingress gates closed, then construct the complete observation image and result record

a nonthrowing serialized commit switches the published revision/epoch/mode/image and active gate table together and reopens admission, and no fallible plugin callback is allowed in the pointer-switch operation
gate checks derive authority from that committed table
no observer or system sees a mixture of old/new assembly
delivery of postcommit notifications is separate and its failure cannot unpublish

if anything fails after the first live write (including ECB playback, allocation, native API or activation gate installation), the world enters Faulted, admission remains closed, no epoch or new snapshot is published and no simulation resumes
its last committed immutable snapshot is inspectable but its live ECS storage is unavailable except to controlled teardown/recovery
V1 does not implement a universal undo journal; recovery recreates a world from a checkpoint or initial definitions, and an external gameplay side effect cannot be erased by this procedure
a partially applied plan is never retried against the same live storage
every state slot identifies (TargetId, OwnerId, SlotId), schema/version, initialization policy, configuration-update policy, owner-transfer policy and last-support-loss policy
existing state defaults to Preserve when the owner/schema stays compatible; a missing compatible policy is a validation error, not implicit zero initialization
a version change uses a registered Migrate function; Reset requires an explicit manifest-supported proposal field and reason
last-support loss MUST declare one of RemoveDerived, PreserveDormant or TransferTo a named available owner with a migration
derived component existence is governed by the union of effective support sets and the slot policy; removing one provider removes exactly its support
final removal is allowed only if no other capability/recipe requires the component; base recipe components are not owned by propagated providers
where one ECS component implements several slots, the generated layout declares a single physical owner and a field mapping, or splits storage
competing arbitrary component initializers are rejected
runtime state is not recomputed from defaults on every assembly diff
each authoritative state domain has one OwnerId and its registered systems may write only their declared slots/components and partitions

multiple systems under that owner need dependency order or provably disjoint generated partitions; V1 accepts disjointness only from validated, mutually exclusive PartitionId assignments, not arbitrary query-predicate claims
overlapping writers from different owners reject assembly
an explicit ownership transfer of a state slot is representable and validated
clauses.note: the transfer expression V1 provides is the state-slot OwnerTransferValidator (P-025/P-032); the writer-domain validator has no transfer input, so a cross-owner writer overlap always rejects. The normative 'unless ownership is explicitly transferred' is a permission, and the obligation it qualifies is the rejection covered by the clause above.

clauses.clause: DI services expose read snapshots and commands, not independent mutable mirrors of ECS state; an engine-owned physical domain is declared as external authority, its ECS data is stamped observation, and ECS submits intent through that adapter
a world is Created -> Running <-> Paused -> Stopping -> Disposed, with Faulted reachable from any nonterminal state and recoverable only through recreation
created worlds become Running only after an initial validated assembly publication

O-26 pauses/resumes at a committed boundary; paused worlds accept bounded queued commands and composition proposals but do not advance simulation; pause/resume changes the separately queried host lifecycle status, not AssemblyEpoch or LogicalStepId
world identity scopes handles, commands, jobs, services, event cursors and resources
world disposal is not scene unload; scene adapters explicitly request the applicable operations
a world chooses FixedStep or CommandDriven at creation; changing it requires checkpoint/recreation in V1

FixedStep configuration declares positive step duration, a scaled/unscaled host clock source and a catch-up limit; the host admits at most the limit per pump, retains remaining debt and emits TimeDebt, never silently increasing step duration or discarding debt
pause freezes simulation accumulation
CommandDriven advances only for accepted commands or explicit registered WakeRequests; no inputs/wakes means zero logical steps
rendering, host callbacks, resource cleanup and composition processing may continue independently, and no kernel rate, turn or physics phase is prescribed
an input cutoff seals each step's batch with a monotonic host-assigned admission sequence

CommandDriven admits one pending command or one wake per logical step by default; a domain can declare an atomic batch envelope as one command; FixedStep consumes the sealed prefix up to its configured capacity and retains the remainder
duplicate request keys return their recorded result, not another execution; a domain rejection still commits an observable rejected command result in a logical step
composition publishes before the next input seal; queued inputs are revalidated against current bindings, schema, authority and target liveness, without retaining stale component pointers
clauses.note: the terminal outcome of a carried or retired row is `Cancelled(RouteRetired)` per P-047; the `Rejected` outcome covers an input refused by admission-time revalidation. The two sentences are reconciled in 00 P-037 (GC-028) and both halves are asserted by the two refusals above.

clauses.clause: terminally invalid inputs finish as Rejected without an empty CommandDriven step
LogicalStepId, fixed-step simulation duration, monotonic host timestamps and plugin-local clocks are distinct
CommandDriven has no implicit elapsed simulation seconds; its commands can explicitly advance domain time
a plugin local clock registers how it advances, pauses and persists and can schedule a typed wake; ordinary wall-clock reads are unavailable inside repeatable rule functions
wake sources have a finite queue/budget and an explicit clock type; pausing cancels/defers wakes according to the declared clock policy; no timer callback mutates ECS directly

a stage declares namespaced StageId, version, owner package, system factory keys, activation membership, Before/After dependencies (required or optional), read/write sets, buffer ports and host affinity
each system entry declares its own access sets and explicit system-key dependencies within its stage

shared stage declarations coalesce only if their contract/version matches; system instances have their own unique keys and declared world/per-partition multiplicity; a world owns at most one system instance per key
missing required stages/systems fail; optional edges disappear when absent
the kernel's boundaries BeginStep and PublishStep are synchronization mechanisms and not game phases
compile stage edges, each stage's internal system DAG, buffer producer-before-consumer edges, structural playback boundaries and explicit owner ordering into a DAG
stage incoming dependencies precede all its root system entries and its outgoing completion follows all leaves; both levels and their access sets enter validation and the plan hash
independent ready nodes are ordered by ascending StageId then system key for trace stability and may execute concurrently
overlapping read/write accesses require a directed path in that expanded DAG or validated disjoint partitions, including systems coalesced into one stage
a write/write or read/write conflict without a semantic edge is AmbiguousOrder; the scheduler MUST NOT invent gameplay order
within a stage, systems can update owned components directly and schedule jobs
the execution driver tracks all handles, including jobs using native containers not tracked by ECS component safety, and no detached job may retain world memory
structural operations record into a declared stage-local deferred buffer and play back after its producers finish and before dependent readers
parallel playback keys use stable target/request order when order is semantically relevant
an ECB/deferred structural buffer is not a gameplay transaction and is not a reason to route all writes through a global queue
clauses.note: P-044 states the same limit from the commit side; the cards suite is the full-domain statement that the transfer is atomic because its owner says so, not because of ECB playback.

clauses.clause: an external CommandEnvelope carries request key (WorldId, IssuerId, IssuerSequence), target stable IDs, payload schema/revision, expected domain version if needed and an admission result token
the host validates envelope/route/capacity and the state owner validates gameplay

a Request is a typed transient inter-system message routed to a named owner and consumer step/stage, not a committed fact; within an active stage owner-internal computation may use direct writes instead of requests, and cross-owner mutation requires a request or explicit transfer contract
RequestResult is Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled or Committed with reason and optional committed event cursor
admission acceptance is not gameplay success

each buffer contract declares schema, lifetime (Stage, Step or bounded NextStep), producer keys, exactly one consuming owner, consumption stage, order key, capacity, overflow behavior and drain/cancel policy
duplicate producers are legal when registered; fan-out uses explicit immutable read ports

clauses.clause: required gameplay input overflow rejects the affected command/batch before mutation; no silent drop
diagnostic/presentation buffers may use explicit lossy policies with counters
no consumer reads a buffer before producer completion; unconsumed step buffers fail commit validation
bounded next-step queues retain stamped stable references and are revalidated after composition changes
cycles between stages/ports require explicit next-step scheduling

clauses.clause: within its declared stage a domain owner may use a finite worklist/reaction loop with explicit ordering, reserved capacity, maximum iterations and prewrite overflow rejection, and it cannot dynamically reenter the stage graph; the kernel neither mandates nor bans bounded same-step domain computation

a plugin may implement multi-entity atomic decisions by gathering intents, validating versions/resources, computing a bounded write set and applying it under its single owner before emitting tentative internal receipts
the kernel does not infer rollback, fairness, economic conservation, combat ordering or atomicity from ECBs

a successful logical step completes all required work, validates required drains, prepares committed events and a consistent snapshot, then nonthrowingly advances LogicalStepId and exposes output together
if unexpected failure follows authoritative writes before that publication, fault the world; do not retry the half-step
postpublication subscriber-delivery errors do not undo the commit
observers see immutable images at (epoch, step) publication only and cannot use inspection to obtain writable ECS references
CommittedEvent records stable IDs, schema/revision, step, epoch, event sequence and causal request
event cursors and snapshots have configured retention bounds; lagging readers receive CursorExpired and resynchronize from a snapshot
internal publication is once per committed operation/step in a live world; subscriber delivery is at-least-once within retention, using (WorldId, event sequence) deduplication
irreversible output adapters consume only committed events, use explicit external idempotency keys and persist an outbox when delivery must survive crashes
installed instances use Registered, WaitingForDependencies, Preparing, Active, Quiescing, Suspended, Retiring, Disposed and Failed
mount is declarative registration plus attempted activation; missing required dependencies yields a published waiting instance with no active contributions, not a half-active plugin

activation requires dependency closure and publication; explicit suspension stops ingress/execution and retracts active contributions using slot policies while retaining installation and configuration, and resume rederives against current ancestry

replacement/reconfiguration stages a candidate activation while the old Active activation continues, and success transitions old -> Quiescing -> Retiring and candidate -> Active at one publication with the installation generation unchanged for an in-place update

voluntary teardown failure before mutation restores old Active gates; failures after mutation follow P-031; failed preparation of a new instance is observable and retryable only by an explicit new operation
quiescing closes new managed callbacks/commands from the retiring activation and freezes affected admission
already executing jobs MUST finish before storage or code-owned resources are released; job cancellation is cooperative intent, not memory reclamation
accepted but unexecuted commands to a suspended/removed route finish Cancelled(RouteRetired) unless the port explicitly declares stable-ID rebinding to a compatible owner
in-flight stage/step execution reaches its commit/fault boundary before composition apply
an async completion with an old epoch is discarded and its staged leases released, even if the stable plugin ID now exists again; callback gates are checked on dispatch and on completion

teardown order is: close ingress; settle current step; fence tracked readers/jobs; retract/publicize the new assembly; retire old resources in reverse dependency order; within an instance dispose leases in reverse acquisition order
dispose each lease at most once, attempt all independent cleanup and aggregate failures
resources still reachable by unfinished work are quarantined and retained; elapsed timeout only reports TeardownBlocked, never authorizes free
retired cleanup failure reports PublishedWithCleanupErrors and keeps tracked quarantined resources, not a false Disposed

a failing subscription disconnector remains behind a closed epoch gate; world shutdown disposes owned ECS storage only after its users end, and a nonterminating native job may require process termination
pre-mutation failure leaves the old published world usable, with staged resources cleaned or quarantined
post-mutation/step failure halts simulation, preserving the last good observation image and fault record

recovery creates a new WorldId from a verified checkpoint or initial catalog, validates/rebuilds composition and recipes, restores state, then reopens admission; old callbacks/handles never become valid
no hidden automatic replay of external side effects is allowed

retryable transient resource failures use host-configured bounded attempts with new operation IDs; correctness failures require changed input/catalog; V1 provides checkpoint recovery, not historical gameplay undo or arbitrary live code replacement
every mutating public operation has an OperationId = (WorldId, IssuerId, IssuerSequence) and canonical input hash; a command's request key is that same operation identity
first submissions from one issuer use strictly increasing sequences across its control operations and commands; retransmissions may reuse earlier IDs
create/restore use a caller-reserved fresh WorldId before allocation and the bounded host ledger retains the reservation through failed/cancelled attempts for its process lifetime
internal suboperations use the parent's operation ID plus a bounded work ordinal

a per-session ledger returns the same pending/terminal result for the same ID/hash and the same retained ID with different input yields IdempotencyConflict; the ledger has configured capacity and terminal entries may be explicitly acknowledged/evicted, after which an absent ID at/below the issuer's retained admission high-water mark returns ResultExpired and cannot execute
issuer high-water marks persist until world disposal; new issuer registration is bounded and old issuer IDs cannot be reused to reset their sequence
restart creates a new world/session and durable replay safety requires the checkpoint/outbox contract

cancellation is accepted before Applying or command execution admission, cleans staged work and returns Cancelled; at/after that cutoff it returns TooLate and the actual operation must be awaited; retrying a rejected revision requires a new operation ID, never mutating the old request
section 10 is the complete V1 kernel operation set; all mutating operations execute on, or enqueue to, the host control lane, and plugins submit proposals rather than calling live ECS mutation APIs
each accepted operation returns a handle immediately, then a terminal result with diagnostic IDs
status/query methods are pure and cancellable without changing the world
unsupported operation variants reject before acquisition

a queued cancellation and publication race is resolved by the serialized control lane at the stated cutoff, never by thread timing inside jobs; failure/cancellation outcomes MUST be observable even when no gameplay step occurs
errors have a stable code, world/operation/plan identity, phase, involved rule/stage/schema IDs, provenance pointers, counts/budgets and retry classification

clauses.clause: a rejection MUST explain the smallest known conflicting set or a bounded summary with retrieval key
logging never changes precedence or world state
checkpoints are taken at a committed boundary after required jobs complete

they contain catalog/protocol fingerprints, world definition/temporal settings, step/time/debt, stable scope/install/target IDs, descriptors, explicit imports/overrides/exclusions, mode, definitions, active and dormant authoritative state, owner versions, RNG streams, bounded pending next-step messages and external outbox/dedup cursors when used
raw host timestamps are normalized to declared clock policy

new host commands wait during capture; already queued external commands are either included with ledger/cutoff or explicitly rejected before capture according to the checkpoint option, never ambiguously omitted
restore validates everything into a new unexposed world before publication

wire/save data uses schema IDs, integer versions, explicit field IDs, canonical byte order, length bounds, null semantics and reference tables; no CLR assembly name or engine handle serves as its identity
unknown required fields/schema versions reject; explicitly optional presentation fields can be skipped
generated serializers and registered directed version migrations replace reflection-based type construction
migration paths must be unique for a requested source/target pair; ambiguity is rejected
pure definitions/rules can be reused elsewhere; Unity assets, Entity layouts, Jobs graphs, physics observations and presentation semantics require engine-specific conversion or reimplementation
V1 protocol is 1.0; manifests declare supported major plus min/max minor and required feature IDs
major changes are incompatible and a minor extension may add optional fields/operations only without changing existing semantics; unknown required features reject before mount
changes to reducers, precedence, stage contracts, serialization or state policy require their own version updates and may require protocol major review
old document compatibility is not a goal, and no runtime silently falls back to Conservative, old combat phases or a different ECS backend on mismatch

registered capability reducers, schemas, state owners, time policies within a selected temporal model, stage contracts, request ports, asset/presentation/input adapters, serializer migrations and pure rule functions are supported V1 seams
trusted extensions still obey memory lifetime, authority, stage access, finite derivation and publication requirements

arbitrary target-generating derivation, runtime code download, security sandboxing, universal engine/ECS adapters, cross-world atomic transactions, distributed consensus and general speculative execution are deferred, not empty mandatory interfaces
a conforming implementation implements all P-001 through P-060, the mandatory operation set, both propagation modes and both temporal models
contract suites use a managed model/oracle; real execution suites use Unity Entities worlds and standalone players; a mock-only implementation or successful compilation is insufficient
the test catalogue and task registry trace every requirement to executable acceptance work
optional gameplay packages do not become kernel dependencies merely because fixtures use them
C# plus Unity Entities is the only V1 ECS backend; Unity Jobs and Burst apply to eligible hot paths and managed composition remains outside Burst
IL2CPP and managed stripping are explicit build acceptance requirements with generated registration/serializer/generic-root coverage
an exact editor/package/native-toolchain baseline is specified in 04
compatibility evidence must include official support constraints and a resolved package lock plus actual player execution; C# syntax or target framework compatibility alone does not pass the gate
the card, narrative and real-time-action reference compositions MUST pass without adding mandatory kernel gameplay schemas or phases
at least cards and narrative execute before provisional generic execution freeze; action and the cross-family composition execute before V1 conformance freeze
each exercises automatic existing/future descendants, mount/unmount, reparent, mode changes, state retention and ownership
a necessary example-specific rule belongs to its package; a general missing mechanism changes this protocol and its tests explicitly
the implementation records the exact build/catalog versions, resolved dependencies, native compiler, architecture, backend/stripping settings, test commands, logs, fixture hashes and measurements
budget numbers are provisional until measured on a named machine

clauses.clause: documentation validation does not imply Unity tests passed and V1 completion requires the dependency-ordered gates, including failures/unload, IL2CPP, checkpoint recovery and no per-frame scope traversal
unknown product platforms/load targets remain explicit, not assumed team size or commercial requirements

clauses.clause: preconditions: serialized control lane; unique session and a supported catalog/profile; no execution before the initial publication
ordering and visibility: invalid catalog rejects without world exposure
failure and cancellation: cancel before allocation publication; repeat returns the same world
postconditions: a new WorldId and a created world whose handles scope to that session (probe: two worlds/restore never share runtime handles)
preconditions: control lane to boundary; same world, parent exists, no ancestry cycle, creation IDs reserved privately
ordering and visibility: a successful publication updates membership and all derived closure together
failure and cancellation: reject a cycle, a cross-world move, a nonempty drop lacking a disposition or a policy conflict; cancel before Applying
postconditions: moving a branch changes inheritance and retains slot state (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: lane, prepare, then boundary; precompiled catalog key and a valid scope with the dependency graph validated and no live callbacks during preparation
ordering and visibility: Active or WaitingForDependencies only after publication
failure: a missing service produces Waiting; an invalid config/graph rejects; a failed new factory reports a Failed attempt
postconditions: one mount changes all eligible existing and future descendants (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: lane to boundary; not Disposed; an explicit suspend flag cleared only on a requested resume; all required dependencies ready
ordering and visibility: staged activation; the epoch changes only on success
failure: still-missing dependencies remain Waiting; a preparation failure retains the prior inactive state; retry needs a new operation
postconditions: a restored provider activates waiting dependents without target wiring (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: prepare while the old activation stays active, then boundary; the installation generation stays unchanged for an in-place replacement
ordering and visibility: schema/owner compatibility and an explicit replacement map validated; the contribution closure is replaced atomically
failure: a missing migration rejects and the old activation remains Active; a postwrite failure faults; cancel before Applying leaves the old activation
postconditions: numerical config changes preserve runtime counters and invalidate late callbacks (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: lane to boundary; the dependency closure is included; ingress closes before the fence
ordering and visibility: Suspended with retained definition/slot dispositions; all contributions from the suspended activation retract
failure: an untransferable state policy rejects while the old activation stays active; a blocked fence stays pending with TeardownBlocked; TooLate after Applying
postconditions: no suspended executor runs and dormant data survives resume (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: lane to boundary, then cleanup; dependents wait or rebind and ownership dispositions apply
ordering and visibility: a removed installation plus a terminal teardown record; no other supports are deleted
failure: a missing required disposition rejects; cleanup errors retain quarantine after a successful publication; repeat retrieves the removal outcome and never recreates
postconditions: one of two supports removed, a committed reward remains and a late callback is discarded (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: lane to boundary with the entire affected closure derived and the setting published with the assembly
ordering and visibility: the same setting with no other edits is NoChange
failure: a conflict or budget rejects while the old mode is retained; cancel before Applying
postconditions: a switch conflict leaves prior capabilities intact and a later spawn follows the committed setting (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control-lane snapshot and pure background work with the strata/index closure and service/execution/state validation complete
ordering and visibility: the plan hash includes all semantic inputs
failure: a pure validation or budget failure has no live effect and same snapshot/input gives the same hash; cancellable between batches
postconditions: the incremental plan hash equals the full oracle (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane or asynchronous I/O with the expected base unchanged, or the plan becomes stale; callbacks gated and resources invisible
ordering and visibility: a validated plan becomes a prepared plan with leases and bounded scratch
failure: missing assets or timeouts release/track staged resources; cancellation is supported until Applying; resources never leak on a failed retry
postconditions: a staged subscription cannot submit gameplay (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: a boundary; seal admission, complete users, recheck the revision, migrate scratch, apply and then expose all tables and the snapshot
failure: a stale plan rejects prewrite; a failed migration retains the old assembly; any postwrite fault halts the world; cancellation is TooLate at Applying
postconditions: a concurrent observer sees exactly the old or the new image, and an injected ECB failure sees neither a partial new image nor resumed execution (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: a boundary via a composition proposal; domain systems request it for the next boundary and never for a recursive closure; spawn uses the current recipe fingerprint
ordering and visibility: the target first becomes query-visible with its complete effective recipe on the first visible epoch
failure: an unknown or stale recipe/handle rejects; cancel before Applying

postconditions: despawn closes the route, fences auxiliaries and destroys only recipe-owned storage (the catalogue's probe: a spawn prepared before a mode/provider edit rederives instead of exposing stale capabilities)
preconditions: control lane; validate world/sequence/schema/route/capacity and dedup before enqueue, with no domain mutation until the admitted step
ordering and visibility: an envelope becomes an admission/result handle
failure: malformed or retired routes reject; a full reliable buffer backpressures; preexecution cancellation returns Cancelled; a duplicate retrieves its result
postconditions: a repeated transfer command changes inventory once (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane then boundary then execution stage; Running with no plan Applying; FixedStep capacity/catch-up or CommandDriven demand; the input prefix is sealed
ordering and visibility: zero or more step attempts
failure: paused or no demand returns NoWork; excessive debt is observable; a timing error rejects the host sample; once executing, cancellation is TooLate
postconditions: one idle second yields zero command-driven steps and a bounded fixed catch-up (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: an execution stage; DAG predecessors and dependencies satisfied, owner/access/epoch valid and all produced handles registered
ordering and visibility: a sealed step, bindings and buffers become tracked jobs and deferred operations
failure: an expected domain rejection emits a result without a write; an unexpected exception after writes faults the step and the world

postconditions: an internal stage cannot independently retry or cancel memory users, and conflicting stages reject at assembly while independent jobs overlap without missing dependencies (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: a boundary; required producers/consumers/structural buffers complete and all public data consistent
ordering and visibility: events and the image are exposed together as a step id, committed events and one snapshot
failure: unconsumed reliable data or a failure faults rather than publishing partial success; a mutated step is never retried
postconditions: a card trade emits no success event on a rejected staged write set (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: any host thread through the synchronized publication pointer; a token retained with no direct mutable state access; disposal releases the lease
ordering and visibility: an immutable lease or page
failure: an expired cursor/token returns an explicit error or resync token and allocation pressure backpressures; read cancellation releases the lease; repeated reads of the same token are identical
postconditions: an observer during a reconfigure never sees a mixed epoch (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane with a known world ledger, decided against the Applying or execution cutoff, with pending staged work invalidated
ordering and visibility: Cancelled or TooLate plus status
failure: an unknown or expired ID is an explicit error; repeated cancel returns the same terminal result; too-late cancellation never implies rollback
postconditions: race permutations produce one legal outcome (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane to boundary; close all ingress, settle jobs, cancel queued commands and retract assembly and reverse dependency resources
ordering and visibility: Stopping then Disposed, or a blocked/quarantined result
failure: repeated stop joins the same attempt; no cancellation once stopping; stuck users remain pinned; cleanup failure is observable
postconditions: a stalled job prevents native buffer free (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: a boundary with stable state, bounded data, an explicit queue/outbox disposition and all required serializers available; copy then serialize off lane
ordering and visibility: a versioned blob and checksum
failure: copy or serialization errors produce no checkpoint; cancel before the completed file publication and remove the temporary artifact
postconditions: active and dormant state round-trip without handles (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane and an unexposed new world reaching a boundary; validate schema/catalog, rebuild identities/composition, repair references and restore state and cursors before Running
ordering and visibility: a new WorldId and a fully published restored world
failure: an unsupported schema/migration rejects without affecting the existing world; cancel destroys the staged world; a duplicate returns the same restored session
postconditions: an old callback cannot target a restored entity (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane; requires an explicit source and reuses the restore/create procedures; old storage never resumes and blocked old resources are retained until safe
ordering and visibility: a stopped old world plus a new session
failure: a failure leaves the old world Faulted and reports the new attempt's failure; no implicit effects replay; cancel only before the new publication
postconditions: a mid-apply fault recovery yields a new identity and the last checkpoint state (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: during prepare or an authorized active control callback with visibility/dependency rules checked and the owner and disposer recorded before the value is exposed

clauses.clause: failure: a conflicting or missing binding rejects; a late acquired result releases immediately; a repeated resource lease request by the same operation/key coalesces
postconditions: disposal happens once and service isolation is unchanged between modes (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane; verify session/generation/activation/operation before installing data; an active gameplay completion becomes a typed command, not a direct ECS write
ordering and visibility: an accepted staged result or a discarded completion
failure: a stale or cancelled result is discarded with cleanup and a duplicate completion idempotently ignores or releases only the newly supplied lease reference, with no auto resurrection
postconditions: 100 late completions yield zero stale writes (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: a pure immutable query that distinguishes published state from staged status explicitly
ordering and visibility: an explanation, status or diagnostics
failure: an expired or unknown token is explicit and cancellation has no semantic effect; the same retained token gives the same explanation
postconditions: every effective capability has complete provenance and losing or excluded candidate reasons (the catalogue's probe)
preconditions: control lane to boundary; only Running<->Paused, waiting for the current step commit or fault first, with commands queueing within capacity while paused

ordering and visibility: a new host lifecycle status plus an unchanged current snapshot token; retained simulation debt with the host-time sample origin reset on resume so paused elapsed time adds no debt; same state returns NoChange and no step or epoch changes merely for pausing
failure: Faulted/Stopping/Disposed rejects; cancellable until the state commit and then TooLate; a repeat retrieves the result
postconditions: a pause during a job waits, a paused duration adds no steps or debt, and a resume processes retained debt and inputs under the usual limits (the catalogue's probe)
clauses.note: 08's phrase "pause while a tracked job is executing" is a Unity-host boundary; the dotnet half proves the job pin and the debt arithmetic, the Unity half proves the host status change does not touch epoch or step. The archive holds no single run that pauses a world with a tracked job in flight (see the task hand-off).
